title: The Always-On Trend Channel
pitch: Content creators lose the trend race in the gap between 'this is blowing up right now' and 'I finally have a video about it.' Chain last30days-skill's cross-platform trend scan (Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, Polymarket) straight into autoclip's link-to-shorts pipeline: every morning the research skill surfaces what's genuinely heating up in a niche, a human (or a second AI pass) turns that into a 60-second script or picks an existing long-form video that covers it, and autoclip renders it into captioned, platform-ready clips for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts before lunch. A solo creator or small agency could run this as a same-day 'trend reaction' content engine for 3-4 niches at once, something no single creator can do by manually scanning forums and editing video themselves.
why_now: Both tools trended today because the same pressure is driving each of them — creators and researchers want less manual grunt work between noticing something and publishing about it — so wiring the noticing tool directly into the publishing tool collapses a day of work into an hour.
